Title: MetaTrans: human drug metabolites
Description: Drugs are reshaped in the liver by phase I and phase II reactions that can blunt efficacy or create toxic metabolites, so the likely products matter early. MetaTrans casts biotransformation as translation, fine-tuning a molecular transformer pre-trained on general chemical reactions with curated human metabolic reactions and combining six fine-tuned models whose predictions are pooled. Decoding uses beam search rather than sampling, so the same input always returns the same metabolites in the same order (up to thirty), with no indication of the enzyme, the rate or whether it accumulates.
Interpretation: Up to thirty human metabolites generated deterministically by beam search from the input compound (most inputs give fewer). Six models each propose five candidates; metabolites are ordered by the best rank at which any model proposes them, then by how many models propose them.
